title: Arcane Conduit
description: Arcane Essence reservoir and spell grid.

settings.label: Verbose
settings.hint: Logs every cast, refusal and queued trigger branch to the SFSE log.

settings.label: Open templates
settings.hint: Opens the template list. Apply, save, rename, delete, or bind F2–F4/F6 combat loadouts without the console.

settings.label: Open spell grid
settings.hint: Opens the hex spell grid.

settings.label: Ammo
settings.hint: Vanilla fuse cell the engine spends per shot (AmmoParticleFuseLight). The plugin watches inventory drop on the SFSE tick -- that drop is the trigger pull. Arcane Essence (Arc_AV_Essence) is the stamina bar; cells only cover fCellCastAssist of each shot's essence bill. RebateEnergyCell refunds mos...

settings.label: Regen Per Second
settings.hint: Optional always-on trickle added to R_grid before f(O2). The old flat regen lived here; the reactor formula below is the real refill now, so this stays 0.

settings.label: Grid Recharge
settings.hint: Arcane resource is a stamina bar, not a magazine. ArcaneRechargeRate = R_grid + R_consumable + R_env EffectiveRecharge  = ArcaneRechargeRate * f(O2) * (exhaustion or 1) Passive fill drains the oxygen bar (fOxygenDrainPerEssence) and stops at fPassiveCap * ArcaneMax. Refill needs equipped grids an...

settings.label: Max Per Grid
settings.hint: Extra ArcaneMax per valid equipped grid. 0 keeps the ceiling at fMaxEssence.

settings.label: Needs Consumable
settings.hint: If true, passive recharge needs a [EssenceConsumables] item in inventory. Default off: mage refill runs on grids + oxygen alone.

settings.label: Cell Cast Assist
settings.hint: Fraction of each shot's essence bill covered by the cell the engine just spent.

settings.label: Oxygen Factor
settings.hint: f(O2) from the oxygen bar: gate (on/off at fOxygenGate), linear (O2/O2max), or soft (smoothstep between fOxygenLow and fOxygenHigh).

settings.label: Oxygen Rate Ref
settings.hint: Oxygen *production* (oxygenRate * oxygenRateMult) as a second multiplier. 0 disables it so f(O2) is purely the bar -- the HUD ring.

settings.label: Oxygen Drain Per Essence
settings.hint: O2 units drained per essence unit passively refilled. Refill also stops when the bar falls below fOxygenMinRefill (fraction of max O2).

settings.label: Passive Cap
settings.hint: Passive sources will not fill above this fraction of ArcaneMax.

settings.label: Diminish
settings.hint: Stacking grid + cells + reactors: extra sources divide the sum.

settings.label: Env Range
settings.hint: Nearby [EssenceReactors] search radius, engine units.

settings.label: Active Siphon Share
settings.hint: Fraction of Horror drain transferred into essence (active refill).

settings.label: Weapon
settings.hint: The WEAP the plugin treats as the spellgun.

settings.label: Modifier Slots
settings.hint: Modifier slots reported to a UI. The grid itself is the real constraint.

settings.label: Rank Actor Value
settings.hint: --- capacity and rank --- Capacity is how much spell the emitter array can physically hold at once. It is not the same thing as essence: essence is what a cast spends, capacity is what the hardware can contain. A spell you cannot afford to cast is still a legal loadout; one that overruns capacity...

settings.label: Rank Capacities
settings.hint: Capacity per rank, rank 1 first. Ranks past the end of the list clamp to the last entry, so adding a Mk VI is an edit here and nothing else. The list is sorted if it is not ascending, since capacity falling with rank would mean a better Conduit holding a smaller spell.

settings.label: Enforce Capacity
settings.hint: Whether an over-budget loadout is refused. Turning this off makes capacity purely advisory, which is useful while retuning the rune tables.

settings.label: Mass
settings.hint: Round mass and muzzle velocity. At the defaults a fresh round carries 0.5 * 40 * 2200^2 = 96.8M energy units, which fEnergyToDamage scales down.

settings.label: Max Damage
settings.hint: Ceiling on one contact, which mostly matters when stacking projectiles.

settings.label: Radius
settings.hint: Contact radius. A round sweeps its whole step, so this is a real thickness rather than a point test, and it cannot tunnel through anybody.

settings.label: Drag
settings.hint: Exponential speed decay per second, and the speed below which the round is no longer a projectile and is retired. Clamped to 90% of fSpeed so a round cannot expire on its first tick.

settings.label: Max Range
settings.hint: Hard limits so nothing lives forever: distance flown, and seconds alive.

settings.label: Launch Height
settings.hint: Launch height above the caster's feet, also used to aim at a body rather than a pair of boots.

settings.label: Energy To Shove
settings.hint: Energy converted into knockback. What the body then hits is priced by [Impact], exactly as with the chain.

settings.label: Hit Cooldown
settings.hint: Seconds a body is immune to the same round. Stops an orbiting round hitting sixty times a second, and stops a pierce round re-hitting what it just left.

settings.label: Max In Flight
settings.hint: Rounds live at once, so a held trigger cannot fill the list.

settings.label: Burst Spread
settings.hint: Cone half-angle, in radians, that a multi-projectile burst is fanned across.

settings.label: Spiral Radius
settings.hint: --- motion rules --- Helix radius and how fast it goes round, in radians per second. A wide slow spiral is a shotgun; a tight fast one is a drill.

settings.label: Homing Turn Rate
settings.hint: Radians per second a homing round can turn, and how far it will look for a target when the caster has no combat target. Keep the turn rate low enough that sidestepping still works -- that is the whole balance of homing.

settings.label: Orbit Radius
settings.hint: Orbit radius around the caster and angular rate, in radians per second.

settings.label: Pierces
settings.hint: --- contact rules --- Bodies a pierce round can cross, and the fraction of speed each one costs. At 0.22, the fourth body is hit at less than half the energy of the first.

settings.label: Bounces
settings.hint: Ricochets allowed, the fraction of speed kept per bounce, and how far it will look for the next target. Restitution is clamped to 1.0: above that a bounce chain would manufacture energy.

settings.label: Cluster Count
settings.hint: Fragments per cluster, their spread, and how long they live. The fragments divide the parent's energy (each leaves at v / sqrt(count)), so raising this makes a cluster wider and softer, never stronger.

settings.label: Energy To Damage
settings.hint: Shared conversions. For a beam the energy is per second; for a pulse it is the whole budget.

settings.label: Beam Power
settings.hint: --- beam --- Power in energy per second. Hold-to-channel (default): the line lives while the trigger is down and dies when you let go. A tap still cooks for fBeamMinDuration so a click is not a one-frame flash. fBeamDuration is the maximum channel (0 = essence tax is the only cap). Auto-fire coal...

settings.label: Beam Length
settings.hint: Length and thickness of the line.

settings.label: Beam Essence Per Second
settings.hint: Essence burned per second while the beam is live. The duration is no longer the only limit: an empty reservoir snaps the line the same way it snaps a reel. Zero disables the tax.

settings.label: Beam Pull
settings.hint: Impulse per second along a pull / push ray. Same units as [Field] fPull. Extra emitters stack linearly. fBeamStopRange is how close a pull will reel before it lets go.

settings.label: Pulse Energy
settings.hint: --- pulse --- The shell's whole energy budget, and how fast it expands in units/second.

settings.label: Pulse Start Radius
settings.hint: The radius the inverse-square falloff is measured from -- anything inside it takes the undiluted budget -- and where the shell dissipates. Must be > 1, since it is the denominator of the falloff.

settings.label: Essence Per Second
settings.hint: Caster tax while any horror is live. Zero disables it.

settings.label: Drain Per Second
settings.hint: Health taken per second from a latched body, and the share fed back to you.

settings.label: Flytrap Vines
settings.hint: Vine-trail flytrap. Nodes along the ground spline; the far node is the maw.

settings.label: Flytrap Charge
settings.hint: Charge telegraph, then jaws open, then snap speed toward the maw (u/s).

settings.label: Flytrap Bind
settings.hint: Bind stiffness (0-1) fed to Kinetics::Solve. Digest hold before the pulse.

settings.label: Tick Interval
settings.hint: How often the payload is applied. The pull runs every frame because it is a rate; the payload cannot -- casting a damage spell sixty times a second would be sixty times the intended effect and would flood the script VM. Floored at 0.05 for the same reason reeling is.

settings.label: Pull
settings.hint: Pull strength at the core, falling off linearly to nothing at the rim. Linear rather than inverse-square on purpose: an inverse square is either negligible at the rim or unsurvivable at the centre, with very little usable range in between. Ignored by plain fields.

settings.label: Hurts Caster
settings.hint: Whether the caster is caught by their own zones. Off by default -- standing in your own cryo storm should be survivable, standing in someone else's should not. When off the caster is excluded from the search itself, so they cannot even be chosen as the pull anchor.

settings.label: Max Zones
settings.hint: Zones standing at once. Each one walks the cell's actor list every tick, so a held trigger must not be able to fill the list. The oldest is dropped rather than the cast refused: the field you just aimed is the one you meant.

settings.label: Essence Per Second
settings.hint: Caster tax while any portal is live. Higher than Horror: a standing hole is expensive to keep.

settings.label: Pull Range
settings.hint: Vortex / ChaosScatter extras. Defaults match Config.h. Pull yanks hostiles toward the disc and spends stored potential. Overspin dumps a slice of spin energy as a radial slash once omega crosses the threshold (bounce and pull spin the blade up). Pierce spells spend arcane for a harder cut (phase...

settings.label: Modifier Key
settings.hint: Key codes are one unified space covering every device: 0-255    keyboard, DirectInput scancodes (Z is 44 / 0x2C) 256-263  mouse buttons (256 left, 257 right, 258 middle) 264-265  wheel up, wheel down 266-281  gamepad buttons Hold the modifier and fire to fuse. Middle mouse by default because it i...

settings.label: Switch Key
settings.hint: Tap this *while the modifier is held* to switch which loadout is live. Z is deliberately chorded rather than taken outright. Z is the hand scanner, and a mod that quietly stole it would be trading one feature for another: with the modifier down it is ours, and without it the scanner works exactly...

settings.label: Suppress Switch Key
settings.hint: Whether the switch key is masked from the game while the modifier is held, so the scanner does not also open when you change loadout. Uses the engine's own disabled-event flag rather than mangling the queue. Turn it off if some other mod needs to see that keypress.

settings.label: Hold Seconds
settings.hint: How long the modifier must already have been down for a shot to count as fused, in seconds. This is what separates a deliberate hold from brushing the middle mouse button. Measured against the engine's own hold accumulator.

settings.label: Tap Seconds
settings.hint: Longest press on the switch key still read as a tap rather than a hold.

settings.label: Capacity Bonus
settings.hint: Capacity budget multiplier while fused. Two loadouts do not get two full budgets: overclocking the array buys headroom, it does not double the hardware. Values below 1.0 are raised to it, since a fused cast with less room than either loadout alone would make fusing strictly worse than not.

settings.label: Min Rank
settings.hint: Rank at which the hardware can resonate two patterns at all. Below it a fused trigger pull falls back to the live loadout rather than failing, so the weapon never simply stops working -- it just does not mutate. Note this must be reachable: at rank 1 with uMinRank=3, fusion is unavailable until t...

settings.label: Essence Per Capacity
settings.hint: Essence charged per capacity point on a fused cast, on top of the spells' own costs. Forcing two patterns through one array wastes essence as heat, so the surcharge scales with how much was forced rather than being a flat tax.

settings.label: Ammo Cost
settings.hint: Extra ammo a fusion burns, for a UI to report. The weapon's own ammo use is the WEAP record's business.

settings.label: Normal Heat Fraction
settings.hint: Share of that heat an ordinary, unfused cast generates. Zero by default: the weapon is meant to be usable indefinitely in its normal mode, and heat is the price of overclocking it rather than of firing it.

settings.label: Sear Fraction
settings.hint: Above this fraction of the ceiling the casing burns whoever is holding it, at fSearDamagePerSecond scaled by how far past the line it is -- so it stings before it hurts.

settings.label: Overheat Damage
settings.hint: One-off damage when the Conduit trips, and how far it must cool before coming back. The restart line is capped below 1.0: at 1.0 it would have to cool to the very line that tripped it and would never restart.

settings.label: Instability Threshold
settings.hint: --- instability --- Misfire chance from running the array near its limit. A misfire spends the essence and the heat and delivers nothing. Note this is deliberately not "capacity used over capacity available" as a raw percentage. Read literally, that makes a legal, fully-packed loadout misfire eve...

settings.label: Misfire Heat
settings.hint: Heat a misfire dumps anyway -- arguably worse than a clean cast, since the energy went nowhere useful.

settings.label: Hostile Range
settings.hint: How far an offensive spell looks for a hostile when the player has no combat target. Self-tagged spells (Arc_Behavior_Self) ignore this and hit the caster.

settings.label: Stiffness
settings.hint: Acceleration per unit of stretch, and the chain's rated speed.

settings.label: Energy To Damage
settings.hint: Kinetic energy -> health. The single empirical constant in the model, and the one number to change if the chain hits too hard or too softly. Calibrated so ONE chain at its rated speed is a solid hit rather than a kill: 1/2 * 80 * 900^2 * 0.0000025 is about 81 health. Stacking chains is then free...

settings.label: Default Mass
settings.hint: Used when an actor reports no mass, which many of them do.

settings.label: Newton Reaction
settings.hint: Newton's third law: the anchor takes an equal and opposite impulse, so chaining something heavy to something light drags the light one.

settings.label: Launch Share
settings.hint: Fraction of the launch energy spent on the wrench itself. The rest is left for whatever the body hits, so the same energy is not billed twice.

settings.label: Stack Efficiency
settings.hint: How much of each additional chain's impulse actually lands. Impulses superpose exactly when the chains pull the same way, so 1.0 is the honest value; anything lower models the slack of chains anchored at slightly different points. Because the speed is linear in the count, the energy delivered gro...

settings.label: Duration
settings.hint: Seconds a hook holds before it lets go on its own.

settings.label: Break Range
settings.hint: Walk further than this from a hooked body and the chain breaks.

settings.label: Reel On Iron Sights
settings.hint: Zooming in reels. This reads the player camera's iron-sights state, which is the first-person aim. If you play in third person and find it does not trigger, bind a key to arc_conduitbridge.SetReelHeld() instead -- the two are ORed, so you can leave this on.

settings.label: Reel Interval
settings.hint: Seconds between reel impulses. One Papyrus dispatch per link per interval, so this is deliberately coarser than a frame.

settings.label: Reel Stiffness
settings.hint: Winch acceleration per unit of distance, and the speed it tops out at. Stiffer than the initial wrench, but rated for the same speed -- it is the same chain. Reeling is harsher because it accelerates faster and keeps pulling, not because the tether suddenly holds more.

settings.label: Reel Stop Range
settings.hint: Stop pulling once the body is this close, so it lands on you instead of grinding into the camera.

settings.label: Reel Ragdoll
settings.hint: Ragdoll a body on the first reel tick. An animated actor largely ignores Havok impulses; a ragdolled one flies.

settings.label: Shaders
settings.hint: --- tether visuals --- There is no chain mesh, and there cannot easily be one: Starfield ships no RFCT records at all, so there is no VisualEffect form to play between two points the way a beam or a rope would be done in an older engine. What is available is an effect shader on the hooked body, w...

settings.label: Hooked Shader
settings.hint: Plays for as long as a body is hooked. Cloned from ReconTargetingFXS -- the "you are marked" look.

settings.label: Reel Shader
settings.hint: Plays on top of the above while the winch is pulling, and comes off the moment you stop aiming. Cloned from ArtifactPower_EarthboundFXS, i.e. gravity.

settings.label: Energy
settings.hint: Starting energy, and the constant that turns it into health. At the defaults a point-blank hit is 240 * 0.55 = 132 at the centre.

settings.label: Decay Time
settings.hint: Seconds for the energy to fall to 1/e (about 37%) of its starting value. This is the single number that decides how quickly the spell stops being worth casting at range.

settings.label: Radius
settings.hint: Starting radius and how fast it grows, in units per second.

settings.label: Max Radius
settings.hint: Ceiling on the radius, so a bolt that lives a long time cannot envelop the district. Raised to fRadius if set lower than it.

settings.label: Speed
settings.hint: Flight speed and the hard range limit. At the defaults the bolt burns out at around 3400 units, so fFizzleFraction is what actually ends most shots.

settings.label: Launch Height
settings.hint: Launch height above the caster's feet, also used to aim at a target's body rather than their feet.

settings.label: Fizzle Fraction
settings.hint: Fraction of its starting energy at which the bolt simply goes out: no blast, no damage, no sound. This is the "tapers off" made literal. 0.0 means it never burns out and only fMaxRange stops it.

settings.label: Max Damage
settings.hint: Ceiling on a single target's blast damage. Mostly matters when stacking projectiles, since each one multiplies the energy.

settings.label: Energy To Shove
settings.hint: Blast overpressure throws bodies; this converts energy into that shove. What they hit afterwards is priced by [Impact], exactly as with the chain.

settings.label: Hurts Caster
settings.hint: Whether your own bolt can catch you. Off by default, which also means you can never detonate one on yourself.

settings.label: Max In Flight
settings.hint: Bolts allowed in the air at once. Further casts are refused rather than silently voiding one already in flight.

settings.label: Medium Radius
settings.hint: --- detonation visuals --- Picked by the blast radius: below fMediumRadius uses the small explosion, below fLargeRadius the medium, above it the large. Three different vanilla fire explosions rather than one record resized, because an explosion's apparent size is its model and particles. These ca...

settings.label: Track Seconds
settings.hint: How long a body stays tracked after an impulse.

settings.label: Min Speed
settings.hint: Below this speed a stop is just a landing, not a collision.

settings.label: Decel Fraction
settings.hint: A collision is a drop to this fraction of peak speed or less.

settings.label: Max Damage
settings.hint: Ceiling on a single impact, so a physics glitch cannot one-shot anything.

settings.label: Radius
settings.hint: Actors this close to the point of impact are counted as having been hit.

settings.label: Transfer Share
settings.hint: Share of the absorbed energy passed to what was struck, before mass ratio.

settings.label: Fall Share
settings.hint: Vanilla already charges for falling, so a purely downward impact is scaled down to this share rather than double-billed.

settings.label: Teleport Distance
settings.hint: Position jumps larger than this are a cell change or fast travel, not motion.

settings.label: Hurts Caster
settings.hint: Whether a body reeled into your face hurts you as well.

settings.label: Native
settings.hint: How a push is delivered. 1 carries the body in the plugin: the impulse Kinetics solved becomes a velocity (v = J/m), and the actor is placed along it every frame. The engine's own impulse call is not in the Address Library, but Actor::SetPosition is a virtual, so this path needs no addresses and...

settings.label: Affects Player
settings.hint: Whether the player can be carried. Off by default: placing the actor the camera is attached to every frame fights both the camera and the controls, and the script path handles that case well enough.

settings.label: Drag
settings.hint: Air resistance, per second, applied exponentially so the result does not depend on frame rate. Higher makes a throw die off sooner, which is what makes distance cost damage rather than just time.

settings.label: Gravity
settings.hint: Downward acceleration in units per second squared while carried. The plugin owns the body's motion for the duration, so this replaces the engine's gravity rather than adding to it.

settings.label: Max Seconds
settings.hint: Longest a single push is carried before the body is handed back.

settings.label: Min Speed
settings.hint: Below this speed the push is spent. Handing the body back here is what stops a shoved actor sliding for the rest of the window.

settings.label: Max Speed
settings.hint: Ceiling on carried speed.

settings.label: Max Step
settings.hint: Furthest one frame may move a body, whatever the velocity says. A dropped frame is otherwise enough to fling somebody through the level.

settings.label: Stop Tolerance
settings.hint: Collision test. The integrator asks for a position and reads back where the body actually got to; falling short by more than the larger of these two means something was in the way, so the carry stops and Kinetics prices the hit. The fraction matters because the tolerable shortfall scales with how...

settings.label: Shove Speed
settings.hint: Speed one point of PushActorAway force stood for. This is [Impact]'s mapping read backwards, so callers that already compute that number keep meaning what they meant.

settings.label: Max Bodies
settings.hint: Bodies carried at once, so a held trigger cannot fill the list. Pushes past the limit fall back to the script path.

settings.label: Prefix
settings.hint: Safety rail, not a convenience. Only records whose Editor ID starts with this are touched, so a typo in a tuning entry cannot silently retune a vanilla record for the whole session. Emptying it disables record tuning entirely rather than allowing everything.

settings.label: Enabled
settings.hint: Community SPELs become runes without an INI edit. Keyword OR prefix.

settings.label: Orbiting
settings.hint: Orbiting: Echoes' Self-centered. Extra spawn count around the origin, billed as capacity because it is another projectile the array has to hold.

settings.label: Orbit
settings.hint: Orbit: capture spawned bodies into a ring. Not extra count, not a SPEL.

settings.label: Non Lethal
settings.hint: NonLethal: grafts Neural Stun onto the branch so kinetics become EM knockout. With Non-Lethal Framework loaded, KO'd humanoids can be restrained.

settings.label: Hailstorm
settings.hint: Mini Meteorite delivery rescales. Same form; these change count, mass, spawn, and guidance. They add no extra SPEL.

settings.label: Frost Helix
settings.hint: Spiral of Cold delivery rescales. Same form; these change omega, icicle rate, vortex, and payload. They add no extra SPEL.

settings.label: Lossy
settings.hint: --- drawback runes --- These add nothing to the spell. Their entire purpose is the negative capacity, and the cost of taking it. Ordered here from mildest to worst bargain: the more capacity a rune returns, the harder it bites. A pure drawback changes no cost, adds no spell and grants no projecti...

settings.label: Heat Leak
settings.hint: HeatLeak: pays in heat, so it only really hurts a fusion build.

settings.label: Unstable
settings.hint: Unstable: pays in wasted casts. The essence and heat are spent either way.

settings.label: Backlash
settings.hint: Backlash: the most capacity any single rune returns, and the worst deal -- hot, unstable, and it does not even reduce the essence bill.

settings.label: Cluster Seed
settings.hint: Cluster Seed: Mini Meteorite as the hanging form bursts from the hit, not from the caster. Same spell, rescaled as a trigger. Consume is the burst's slice of stored kinetic/thermal potential.

settings.label: Shard Burst
settings.hint: Spiral of Cold on-hit triggers. Hanging form spawns at the icicle/segment strike, not at the caster. Consume is the child's slice of stored potential.

settings.label: On Spawn
settings.hint: Spawn: Rolling Stone / Spiraling Rage. The boulder is whatever form you hang on the branch, billed as capacity because it is a second complete spell. Consume is 0: the parent has not stored potential yet.

settings.label: After Range
settings.hint: Distance: farther the parent flies, the more times this fires, up to 3. 900u is a short throw on a bloom and a long one on a contact bolt.

settings.label: Overstrain
settings.hint: Tension: the chain is pulling harder than 700 u/s (rated cap is 900). Pulse: 40% of stored tension/inertia becomes the hanging shockwave.

settings.label: At Speed
settings.hint: Speed: a thrown or reeled body is flying faster than 900 u/s.

settings.label: On Snap
settings.hint: Snap: leftover essence converts when the DEST body breaks. Consume 0 so Construct::Burst is the only spender of that leftover.

settings.label: Held Mass
settings.hint: Mass: the field is holding more than a heavy body and a half.

settings.label: Overcharge
settings.hint: Potential: the field has stored enough leftover to dump a real blast.

settings.label: Cracking
settings.hint: Durability: the DEST body is down to a third. Hang a slam or scatter here.

settings.label: Sluggish
settings.hint: --- limiting triggers --- Sluggish: the branch lands eventually. Long enough to matter, cheap enough to be worth it when you need the capacity elsewhere.

settings.label: Faltering
settings.hint: Faltering: fires once, very late, and only when you are nearly dry.
